name: Tumble Dryer
description: A standard heat-pump or condenser tumble dryer. One of the highest-wattage everyday appliances — ideal candidate for load-shifting.

name: Washing Machine
description: A typical front-loader washing machine. Less powerful than a dryer but still worth shifting overnight.

name: Washer-Dryer Combo
description: A combined washer-dryer runs a full wash and dry cycle back-to-back. Longer runtime makes it especially worth scheduling overnight.

name: Dishwasher
description: Most modern dishwashers have a delay-start feature — perfect for running at greenest hours overnight.

name: Electric Oven
description: A conventional electric fan oven. High wattage but short run time — great for batch cooking during a cheap Agile window.

name: Microwave
description: A standard 900W microwave. Short bursts of use — scheduling individual runs isn't practical, but using it during cheap windows adds up.

name: Kettle
description: The humble kettle is the UK's highest-wattage small appliance. Each boil uses about 0.15 kWh — its impact comes from frequency, not duration.

name: Air Fryer
description: More efficient than a full oven for smaller meals. Scheduling a batch cook during a cheap half-hour slot is straightforward.

name: Bread Maker
description: Bread makers have a delay-start timer — set them up in the evening and schedule the bake for the cheapest overnight window.

name: Slow Cooker
description: Very low wattage but long run times. Scheduling a slow cooker during low-carbon daytime windows is an easy win.

name: Coffee Machine (bean-to-cup)
description: Bean-to-cup and espresso machines draw significant power during heating. Scheduling the warm-up in a cheap slot cuts costs.

name: EV Charger (7 kW home unit)
description: A standard home wallbox (32A, 7.4 kW). Run duration depends on how many kWh you need — adjust using the target kWh field.

name: EV Charger (3 kW slow)
description: A 3-pin or slow 13A charge, common in older homes without a wallbox installed.

name: EV Charger (22 kW three-phase)
description: Three-phase AC charger common in new-builds and commercial properties. Charges most EVs from empty in under 2 hours.

name: Storage Heater
description: Off-peak storage heaters designed to charge overnight and release heat through the day — core Economy 7 appliance.

name: Immersion Heater (hot water tank)
description: Heating a hot-water cylinder with an electric immersion element — commonly paired with Economy 7 or solar diverters.

name: Air Conditioner / Portable AC
description: Portable or window AC units. Running during low-carbon early-morning hours before the day heats up can significantly reduce your carbon footprint.

name: Air Source Heat Pump
description: Air source heat pumps are 3–4× more efficient than direct electric heating. Scheduling pre-heating during cheap overnight windows maximises savings.

name: Fan Heater
description: An electric fan heater provides instant heat but is relatively expensive to run. Use sparingly and pick the cheapest window.

name: Dehumidifier
description: Dehumidifiers can run unattended for long periods. Scheduling them overnight in low-intensity windows keeps running costs minimal.

name: Electric Shower
description: A 9.5 kW electric shower is the highest-wattage appliance in most UK homes. Each 10-minute shower uses about 1.6 kWh.

name: Hair Dryer
description: A typical 2 kW hair dryer used for 10 minutes. Brief but high-wattage — morning peak usage adds up over a household.

name: Swimming Pool Pump
description: Pool circulation and filtration pump. Typically runs 8+ hours a day — running it in low-carbon overnight windows can cut CO₂ significantly.

name: Hot Tub / Spa
description: Hot tubs heat and circulate water continuously. Scheduling heating cycles during cheap overnight windows is one of the biggest residential savings opportunities.

name: Fridge-Freezer
description: A modern A-rated fridge-freezer runs continuously but compressor cycles are short. Annual consumption is around 150–250 kWh.

name: Chest Freezer
description: Chest freezers are among the most efficient cold appliances — typically using under 100 kWh per year.

name: Gaming PC
description: A mid-range gaming PC with a discrete GPU under load. Scheduling longer gaming or rendering sessions for cheap windows can save noticeably.

name: Desktop Computer
description: A typical office or home desktop computer. Low wattage but often left on for hours — overnight scheduling of updates and backups helps.

name: Home Server / NAS
description: Network-attached storage or home server running 24/7. Scheduling intensive tasks (backups, transcoding) for green windows makes a cumulative difference.

name: 3D Printer
description: FDM 3D printers run unattended for hours. Scheduling overnight prints during cheap Agile windows is an easy efficiency win.

name: Robot Vacuum
description: Most robot vacuums are schedulable via app. Setting them to run during the cheapest morning window is a simple set-and-forget saving.

name: Infrared Sauna
description: Home infrared saunas heat up in 15–20 minutes and draw around 1.6–2.4 kW. Scheduling the warm-up during a cheap half-hour window cuts cost and carbon.

name: Home Battery System
description: Home battery systems (e.g. Powerwall, GivEnergy) charge from the grid during cheap off-peak hours to power the home during peak times.
